pr_title: client-go: share the same transport for generated clientsets
pr_body:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup

Until now, when creating a Kubernetes Clientset, a new RESTClient was created per group/version. Since RESTClient transport can not be cached in some occasions, i.e. when using a custom transport, this has the consequence that each group/version had an independent TCP connection to the API server.

Since the Transport, of the RESTClient can be shared when creating a global Kubernetes Clientset, this PR adds a new RESTClient constructor `RESTClientForConfigAndClient` to allow to generate clientsets using the same http client.

Fixes #91913, #103225

```release-note
client-go uses the same http client for all the generated groups and versions, allowing to share customized transports for multiple groups versions.
```

> is describe constructing a new client per described object

this seems to be the case (i wrote my stream of consciousness notes below). i am having trouble understanding why we need a new client per described object...do you have any historical context here/thoughts of why this would be the case?

---

1. for each of the `pods`, we create a `describe.ResourceDescriber`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go#L179
2. for each `describe.ResourceDescriber`, we create a `*kubernetes.Clientset`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L160
3. for each `*kubernetes.Clientset`, we create a client for each API version: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/clientset.go#L370
4. for each API version client, we create a `*rest.RESTClient`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/typed/apps/v1/apps_client.go#L67
5. upon creation, a `*rest.RESTClient` transitively calls `exec.Authenticator.UpdateTransportConfig()`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/exec/exec.go#L203

my estimation is that the number of times that `exec.Authenticator.UpdateTransportConfig()` is called is `O(nm)` where `n` is the number of `pods` and `m` is the number of per-API version clients.

i count 41 per-API version clients in a `*kubernetes.Clientset`. when i have 36 pods, i see the warning message show up for 1515 clients. 36 * 41 = 1476 which is close enough to 1515 to make me think that the above estimation is correct.

I do not think there is any way for `UpdateTransportConfig` to know when the associated client is no longer needed (and I do no think we can ignore the input `c.Dial` in an attempt to share a single dialer across all clients).  That is, `onRotateList` grows without bound and we "leak" clients.  A bandage solution would be to cache the `describer` based on the `mapping` (in a function local map):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go#L178-L179

This is a one-off solution for describe, and does not help in the general case of "bad things happen when you make too many clients and immediately throw them away."

In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in `tlsCache`.

> this seems to be the case (i wrote my stream of consciousness notes below)

nice investigation, thanks!

> A bandage solution would be to cache the `describer` based on the `mapping` (in a function local map)

We should do *something* to improve describe (even if we're also able to improve the tlsCache hits)... constructing 1500 clients to describe 40 pods is egregious, and just figuring out the inputs to determine a tlsCache hit is more expensive than I'd want to pay 1500 times.

> This is a one-off solution for describe, and does not help in the general case of "bad things happen when you make too many clients and immediately throw them away."
> 
> In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in `tlsCache`.

I agree it would be good to improve this, though the ability to compare opaque inputs for cache-hit purposes is limited.
Seems like a least common denominator here is to fix the describe behavior so that it doesn't create so many clients. I'll try to see if I can improve on that for starters.

I was able to reproduce that `get` behavior. I created around 1000-ish (1094 to be exact) `configmaps` in a single namespace, ran `kubectl get configmaps -o yaml`, and saw those warning messages.

---

Currently I partition this GH issue up into 3-ish chunks, in order from most egregious to least egregious:
1. `kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go` should not be creating a client for every object it wants to describe
1. `In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in tlsCache` (from @enj's comment[0] above)
1. `get` should not be creating a client for every object it wants to print out (I didn't actually see this in the code, but it does seem like this is what is causing those warnings to show up when dealing with 1000+ objects)

- For `#1`, I feel like we could implement the bandage solution @enj suggested above (i.e., function-local cache of `describe.ResourceDescriber`) since this would be a net improvement on the `describe` code. I will open a PR to do that.
- For `#2`, I am still scratching my head, because coming up with a cache key for this seems hard (a la @liggitt's) note above[1]. I will focus on `#1` for now and then come back to this one.
- For `#3`, I wonder if we could do something similar to what we do for `#1`. I will open up a fix for `#1`, have it go through review, get it merged in, and then figure out if we want to generalize the fix to work for `#3`. I feel like we should fix `#2` before we fix `#3`, though, since `#2` is the root of the evil.

[0] strawperson proposal: do nothing
- i thought about this all afternoon yesterday, and i feel like since we want 1) our exec plugin code to be able to close connections for those clients when certificates rotate (which seems absolutely necessary from a system resource perspective) and 2) a 1:many relationship between `exec.Authenticator`'s and clients (which seems desired from a memory usage perspective and synchronization perspective), and 3) we want to abstract our `exec.Authenticator` `RoundTripper` code from underlying L4 details, then we are stuck with this problem of needing to keep an ever growing list of connection information
- the more i think about this, the more i think that the real issue here is that we are creating >1000 clients in some places
- 1000 clients is a lot - seems like this should only be necessary when you have 1000 distinct API endpoints that need some sort of network isolation (e.g., flow control)
- to my knowledge, kube does not have 1000 distinct API endpoints that would need individual clients

[1] strawperson proposal: reuse same `rest.RESTClient` for each `schema.GroupVersion`
- looks like we are creating a new client for every resource in `kubectl get <resource> -o json`
- we pass a function pointer into a `resource.mapper` tha runs for every resource: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5150d2f8394a35dbe6621e4589cab97935d1ecc7/staging/src/k8s.io/cli-runtime/pkg/resource/builder.go#L286
- maybe we could have a per-`resource.mapper` cache that caches clients per `schema.GroupVersion`?
- i'll open another pr for this (EDIT: here is the PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97855)

[2] strawperson proposal: do nothing (EDIT: do https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97821)
- if i understand correct, a `rest.RESTClient` needs to know which `schema.GroupVersion` it is talking to so that it knows how to read/write stuff from/to the wire: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc09a6df5805574394e2eff285756d2886b34805/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/client.go#L68
